methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $83M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Verse is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $83.3M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of three same-sector, adjacent-stage private companies—KoBold Metals (Series C, $3.0B), Electric Hydrogen (Series C, $1.0B), and Amogy (Series C, $700M)—alongside one public comparable and eight additional private peers in the energy transition space.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, yielding $158M. Peer-median analysis anchors to the median valuation of the three same-sector comparables at $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. These methods reflect materially different assumptions about Verse's development trajectory relative to later-stage peers.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $135M to $1.1B, with a median of $579M. The wide spread reflects two key uncertainties: first, the stage gap between Verse (Series B) and the peer set (predominantly Series C), which meaningfully influences terminal value assumptions; second, the application of stage-progression methodology versus market multiples on fundamentally different bases. A refined valuation would benefit from Verse-specific metrics on capital efficiency, unit economics, or technology differentiation relative to these peers.
